text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Private supermarkets chain Leclerc opens its first European purchasing center in Zurich and allies with German Markant in European Marketing Distribution, Europe's first network of independent retailers.
-- Member of parliament calls for a tender to allocate the real-estate loan activity from Credit Foncier.
-- Canadian report hints the French overestimate dangers linked to asbestos exposure.
-- A rise of the dollar to near 5.40 francs is expected to support French economic growth.

-- Government ready to alter a 1937 banking sector decree to introduce greater flexibility in opening hours, in agreement with unions. Finance minister Jean Arthuis and labour minister Jacques Barrot agree on project.
-- Continuous and steady rate cuts have allowed banks to enjoy a boom in their financial market activities in 1996.
-- SNCF railroad operator expects price hikes on long-distance services.

-- Budget deficit at end November reached 329.4 billion francs, far from a 288-billion-franc target for 1996 as a whole, but the government remains confident that December figures will make up for gap.
-- Local authorities to implement new legal measures to limit vehicle traffic at times of air pollution peaks.
-- Workers at auto parts maker Valeo 's Normandy plant to fight against a planned closing of their plant, which manufactures headlights.
-- Shares of media group Havas rose 11 percent on talk it would buy an outstanding 26 percent stake in publisher CEP Communication.
